trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any credible IPO/valuation headline (S-1 filing, funding round repricing) coincides with the probability move; absent news, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT intraday move vs. QQQ/SOX to see if any idiosyncratic AI-valuation bid is present.
time_plan.2h: Re-examine which adjacent bracket (>$1T or <$750B) lost probability to infer implied direction of OpenAI valuation.
time_plan.6h: Scan for private-market secondary pricing or SoftBank/Thrive round leaks that would justify a real revaluation.
time_plan.12h: Assess whether MSFT and AI-complex closed with any durable move attributable to OpenAI valuation news; if not, log as non-tradable.

predictions.reasoning: OpenAI is privately held with no listed shares, so this market cannot move an OpenAI security directly. The most exposed liquid proxy is Microsoft, which holds a large economic interest in OpenAI. A shift in the implied probability of a specific $750B–$1T IPO-day cap bracket is only weakly informative: it is a narrow range bet contingent on (a) whether an IPO even happens by end-2026 and (b) where the cap lands within many possible brackets. Higher implied OpenAI valuation could be mildly positive for MSFT's stake mark, but a move INTO this specific middle bracket is directionally ambiguous — it could reflect valuation being revised down from >$1T or up from <$750B. Net near-term read-through to MSFT over a 12h window is essentially noise.

llm_justification.summary: This market prices a narrow $750B–$1T bracket for OpenAI's IPO-day market cap, with resolution possible as far out as end-2026. OpenAI is private, so there is no direct tradable asset, and the only meaningful public proxy is Microsoft via its economic stake. A move in this specific middle-bracket probability is directionally ambiguous (it could reflect valuation being marked up from below or down from above) and is far too diffuse over a 12-hour window to imply a tradable move. Mapping is weak; direction unclear and confidence low.
key_assumptions: Microsoft is the best available liquid proxy for OpenAI valuation sentiment
Bracket probability shifts do not carry clean directional information
No imminent IPO catalyst within the 12h window
failure_modes: The proxy (MSFT) is only fractionally exposed to OpenAI's mark and dominated by its own fundamentals
A bracket move reflects mechanical repositioning, not new information
Any real valuation news is likely already public before the market moves
The event may never resolve to an IPO at all, making asset read-through moot
Attributing any MSFT move to this market is likely spurious correlation
